records.supported_name_scope: American Creek is supported for the eastern headward stream and the long northern and western creek corridor. The selected named lake passages are Murray Lake, Hammersly Lake, Lake Coville, Lake Grosvenor and the connected Naknek Lake complex. The route includes only the lower Savonoski River below the southern Grosvenor outlet setting, then Naknek River below Naknek Lake. The separate names of the short Coville–Grosvenor connection and southern Grosvenor outlet reach are not established.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected eastern start follows American Creek northwest into Murray Lake and Hammersly Lake, then turns west along American Creek, makes its large northern bend and descends south into Lake Coville. It passes southeast through the Coville–Grosvenor connection, east along Lake Grosvenor and south around its eastern end. From the southern Grosvenor outlet and Hardscrabble tributary-mouth setting it reaches the Savonoski River, follows the lower Savonoski southwest and enters the southeastern arm of the Naknek Lake complex. It continues west across that arm, northwest through the connecting narrows, and west across the main lake to its western outlet. The second fragment continues through the Naknek River bends past King Salmon toward Naknek. The selection excludes the upper Savonoski approaching from the east, the upper Hardscrabble valley, the Brooks River/Lake Brooks branch and the separate Nonvianuk Lake drainage to the north.
records.region: Southwestern Alaska, from the American Creek headward valley in the Walatka Mountains through Katmai lake country to the lower Naknek River at Naknek.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity for the selected American Creek, lake-chain, lower Savonoski, Naknek Lake and lower Naknek River route.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded creek, lake, receiving-junction and lower-river correspondence for both selected fragments against two acquired original USGS National Map raster exports. The whole-route image covers the complete selection; an eastern enlargement resolves the initial American Creek lake sequence and the southern Grosvenor/Savonoski connection. Original source pixels and separate local orientation overlays were inspected across the entire route. This establishes the generalized waterway and lake sequence, not exact banks or channel threads. In particular, the modeled exit from southern Lake Grosvenor crosses the Hardscrabble tributary-mouth/floodplain setting east of the mapped short lake-outlet channel; the actual outlet connection to Savonoski is visible, but the modeled line is not an exact trace of that outlet. No separate outlet name or upstream Hardscrabble identity is inferred.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component: Selected American Creek reach southeast of Murray Lake; not an official source-point determination.
naming_scope_details.upper_named_component: American Creek, with separate Murray Lake and Hammersly Lake passages, followed by the northern bend and lower creek into Lake Coville.
naming_scope_details.intermediate_named_river_component: Lower Savonoski River below the southern Lake Grosvenor outlet setting.
naming_scope_details.lower_river_component: Naknek River below the western Naknek Lake outlet, through King Salmon to the lower reach at Naknek.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Lower Naknek River at the Naknek settlement setting, within the river rather than an exact bay shoreline.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply Naknek River uniformly to American Creek, the named lakes, the short interlake/outlet passages or lower Savonoski River.

The modeled southern Grosvenor exit crosses the Hardscrabble tributary-mouth/floodplain setting. This does not establish Hardscrabble Creek as the name of the lake outlet or authorize substitution of its upper tributary valley.
Repeated river-network labels over mapped lake interiors do not replace the distinct lake identities.
Do not substitute the unselected upper Savonoski, Brooks River/Lake Brooks branch or Nonvianuk drainage for the selected route.

No separate name is established for the Coville–Grosvenor connector, southern Grosvenor outlet or southeastern Naknek Lake arm. No Indigenous alternative name, legal naming date or Korean name is established.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 283.298 km modeled length describes this selected two-fragment creek–lake–river route, not an official length of Naknek River or American Creek. The line generalizes lake crossings, shore geometry, braided channels and bends, with an especially visible lateral simplification in the southern Grosvenor outlet/floodplain setting. Actual connected corridor correspondence is supported; exact channel alignment is not. No geometry modification or point-by-point geometry revalidation was performed.

records.supported_name_scope: Original federal cartography supports Rivière Sainte-Marguerite, Lac aux Cèdres, Petit lac des Cèdres, the Lac Carré setting and Réservoir de la Sainte-Marguerite 3. Provincial engineering records distinguish the Denis-Perron, Sainte-Marguerite-2 and Sainte-Marguerite-1 installation settings on the same river. The initial feeder and a separate official name for the lower impounded water body are not established.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The western headward approach runs east through small waters to the upper Sainte-Marguerite corridor, then turns south through the Cèdres lakes. The route continues southeast past the Lac Carré setting, south through the long Sainte-Marguerite 3 reservoir and its southern bend, then follows the downstream canyon southeast before turning south and southwest along the lower impounded valley. It passes the Clarke City setting and ends near the inner estuarine bend toward Val-Marguerite and Baie Sainte-Marguerite. The Cacaoui, Dumas, Vallée and de la Coulée tributary approaches are not substituted for the selected trunk. This is the Côte-Nord river west of Sept-Îles, not another Québec river of the same name.
records.region: Québec Côte-Nord, south from the western upper Sainte-Marguerite lake country through the Monts Groulx valley to Clarke City and Val-Marguerite west of Sept-Îles.
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river identity for the selected western headward feeder, named upper lake passages, Sainte-Marguerite 3 reservoir corridor and lower regulated river.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded route and component correspondence for both selected fragments. Five original federal raster exports cover the whole selection and overlapping headward, upper-transition, reservoir and lower-river enlargements. Original pixels were read separately from local orientation overlays. The larger-scale reservoir depictions were used to resolve the small-scale layer's older narrow-river representation. Provincial dam records independently fix the regulated-reach settings. The result establishes the selected waterway sequence, not exact banks, current water levels, surveyed dam crossings or exhaustive minor hydronyms.

naming_scope_details.initial_headward_component: Unnamed western lake-and-stream approach to the upper Sainte-Marguerite corridor.
naming_scope_details.lower_impounded_component: The selected widened lower valley upstream of Barrage Sainte-Marguerite-2. Its physical correspondence and dam relationship are supported; no separate official reservoir name is assigned from the blank provincial field or unlabeled federal water polygon.
naming_scope_details.lower_river_component: Rivière Sainte-Marguerite through the Clarke City and inner estuary approach.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Inner lower-river bend toward Val-Marguerite, upstream of the remainder of the estuary and Baie Sainte-Marguerite.
excluded_inferences: Do not apply the representative river name uniformly to the unnamed initial feeder, named lake components or reservoir passages.
Do not substitute a conventional northern source description or a side tributary for the actual selected western approach.
Do not treat the model fragment split inside the reservoir as an official hydronym boundary.
Named bays, portages, terrain features and tributaries shown next to the route are not aliases of the whole river or reservoir.
The map's Lac Carré label is preserved as a named setting within the connected upper corridor; no legal lake-to-reservoir boundary or unaltered historical shoreline is asserted.
No legal naming date, exhaustive minor-water inventory, Indigenous-name equivalence or Korean name is established. Canadian gazetteer and CGN records were not requested or used.
naming_scope_details.source_scale_limit: The small-scale overview shows a narrow river where larger-scale map exports show the Sainte-Marguerite 3 impoundment. The detailed water polygons, connected-route evidence and readable reservoir label govern the component interpretation. The composite service does not provide a single compilation date; no current operational water level or engineering status is inferred.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 283.136 km value is the modeled two-fragment route length, not an official river length. Generalized segments cross meanders, lake edges and reservoir waters approximately. No geometry alteration or point-by-point survey alignment is proposed.

records.supported_name_scope: IGN directly labels A. El Cano on the western approach, A. de Tegua farther east, A. Chazón in the middle-eastern lowland, and Bañados del R. Saladillo at the selected ending. These are component or receiving-landscape names rather than interchangeable full-route river names. A separate modern primary study establishes regional canalized integration of the Chazón system; it does not resolve the exact selected terminal trace.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The sole selection begins in the El Cano setting south of Río de los Sauces, follows the El Cano corridor east and southeast across the road/rail corridor north of Alcira Gigena, then turns northeast along Tegua past Santa Bárbara Sur, Las Selvas and Punta del Agua. It crosses the low country through La Paulina and Dalmacio Vélez Sársfield, then turns south west of Ticino through Las Chilcas and La Mala Vuelta. The route reaches the mapped Chazón corridor near Los Granaderos and La Magdalena, passes west and south of Etruria, bends east of Chazón village, and crosses the rail/road corridor west of Pascanas. It continues south through La Uruguaya, Sol de Mayo, El Nido and La Cordobesa surroundings into the Bañados del Río Saladillo east of La Carlota. It does not follow the separate Río Cuarto mainstem through La Carlota, the Carnerillo western approach, or the Río Tercero–Carcarañá trunk.
records.region: Central-southern Córdoba, Argentina: El Cano and Tegua country, Alcira Gigena, Punta del Agua, Dalmacio Vélez Sársfield, Etruria, Pascanas and the Bañados del Río Saladillo.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic and name-scope comparison of the entire retained selection with a readable original IGN 1:250,000 raster, overlapping local enlargements and private orientation overlays, the retained original IGN Córdoba physical map, and original figures 1 and 3 plus relevant hydrological text in an independent 2020 field-study article. No selected interval is obscured by missing raster coverage. The unresolved issue is attribution of the modeled wetland/connector trace, not unreadable geography or denial of all regional hydrological integration.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The readable maps establish named headward and middle components and a terminal wetland setting, while the independent modern study establishes regional canalized Chazón-system integration. They do not establish that the exact modeled connectors and southern terminal leg constitute one compatible, fully attributable named river route. The hold is narrower than a claim of regional hydrological disconnection and is not merely caused by different component names.

naming_scope_details.headward_component: A. El Cano followed by A. de Tegua in the original IGN topography.
naming_scope_details.middle_component: Marshy and partly canalized Tegua–Chazón lowland, with a directly labeled local A. Chazón corridor; regional Chazón-system integration is independently documented.
naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Bañados del Río Saladillo east of La Carlota; no precise named receiving-channel junction established at the selected endpoint.
excluded_inferences: Do not extend El Cano or Tegua over all 283.055 km.
Do not rename all selected marsh connectors Chazón solely from regional basin integration.
Do not describe the entire route as a continuous natural river, or infer continuous contemporary flow from modeled geometry.
Do not claim the regional Tegua–Chazón systems are disconnected: independent primary research establishes canalized integration.
Do not turn the wetland name Bañados del Río Saladillo into an alias for the selected full river group.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The inventory length describes the modeled route. It is not an official river length, surveyed channel alignment or evidence for precise current channel connectivity. Historical topographic and modern engineering-channel configurations differ.

records.supported_name_scope: Readable IGN topography establishes a plains/low-depression route through agricultural country, marshes and lagoons, ending in Laguna Las Tunas Grandes after crossing the Laguna El Hinojo setting. It does not depict or label a single continuous natural river along the complete selection. Hydronyms for the unidentified headward and intervening connectors remain null.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The sole selected path begins near Estancia San Hilario south of Adolfo Van Praet, bends north to the rail corridor near Aguas Buenas, then south and east through the Las Mellizas, La Voluntad and Ramón Segundo surroundings south of Coronel Hilario Lagos and Mariano Miró. It turns northeast toward Sarah and Bernardo Larroudé, then southeast through the Trequén and El Meridiano lowlands, crossing into Buenos Aires and passing Villa Sauze. It continues south through the Colonia San Francisco surroundings, east of González Moreno, crossing the road/rail corridor at San Mauricio west of América. Farther southeast it passes the La Colorada and La Criollita surroundings toward Fortín Olavarría, then the La Cristina–San Miguel lagoon setting and the plains through La Chiquita, Los Quilmes and El Refugio. The lower line crosses north of Trenque Lauquen and through the El Refugio–La Lomita surroundings, crosses the mapped road and railway corridor near La China and Los Chañares, traverses Laguna El Hinojo, and ends within the mapped Laguna Las Tunas Grandes surface east of the city. The modeled lake crossings do not define a surveyed wet channel or the present shoreline.
records.region: Northeastern La Pampa and western Buenos Aires, Argentina: Adolfo Van Praet, Coronel Hilario Lagos, Sarah and Bernardo Larroudé, Villa Sauze, San Mauricio, Fortín Olavarría, Trenque Lauquen and the Hinojo–Las Tunas lake complex.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded geographic and name-scope review of the entire actual selected path against a single original IGN 1:250,000 map response with complete coverage, overlapping northern, border, middle and southern crops, and private orientation overlays. The province's independently read hydrological overview supplies regional context. No selected interval is hidden by a missing sheet or unreadable raster. The hold concerns unsupported whole-route river identity and connector continuity, rather than incomplete map access.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: Complete readable primary cartography locates the selection through northern plains, long inter-depression connectors and a named terminal lake complex, but supplies no single compatible named natural river or verified named receiving-river route across the whole selection. The independent regional overview confirms that drainage is strongly shaped by depressions and canals. Those regional relationships do not resolve the exact modeled connectors; unknown names remain null.

naming_scope_details.terminal_component: Mapped Laguna El Hinojo crossing and Laguna Las Tunas Grandes ending; lake names, not a named river trunk.
excluded_inferences: Do not assign Río Quinto or Río Salado from a regional hydrological association or lake destination.
Do not label the entire selection Canal Norte or Jauretche–Mercante solely from nearby or regional engineering works.
Do not treat modeled links across farmland, depressions and lakes as proof of one continuously flowing natural river.
Do not assert permanent dryness, lack of modern canals, or absence of episodic regional hydraulic connections.
Do not convert Laguna El Hinojo or Laguna Las Tunas Grandes into river-name aliases.
naming_scope_details.model_limits: The 281.98 km figure is the inventory's modeled-mainstem length. Historic mapped shores and the generalized line do not establish exact present water boundaries, channel positions, flow direction at every connector, or a contemporary surveyed outlet.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Keep the saved order unchanged and use later result IDs/status changes to mark progress. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated; no lake research until all river continental phases have had their review pass.
